full_parsed_json.title: The interval conjecture for second-level universal lower bounds
full_parsed_json.statement:
For each dimension $n$, let $D(n,\tau)$ and $D(n,\tau+1)$ be the endpoint cardinalities associated with consecutive levels, and consider those $N$ in the interval

$$
N\in [D(n,\tau),D(n,\tau+1)]
$$

for which second-level bounds exist.

**Interval conjecture.** For every dimension $n$, the values $N\in [D(n,\tau),D(n,\tau+1)]$ for which second-level bounds exist form an interval.

The conjecture concerns the observed organization of second-level universal lower bounds across cardinalities; the source formulates it as a concluding conjecture and provides examples, but no resolution.
full_parsed_json.source_name: Peter Boyvalenkov, Peter Dragnev, Douglas Hardin, Edward Saff and Maya Stoyanova, “Universal bounds for spherical codes: the Levenshtein framework lifted”, arXiv:1906.03062 (2022).
full_parsed_json.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.03062

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2019).

full_parsed_json.title: The independence-number bound for clique immersions
full_parsed_json.statement:
Let $G$ be an $n$-vertex graph, and let $\alpha(G)$ denote its independence number. **Independence-number clique immersion conjecture.** The graph $G$ contains

$$
K_{\lceil n/\alpha(G)\rceil}
$$

as an immersion.

This conjecture extends Vergara's conjecture from independence number $2$ to arbitrary independence number. The bound is motivated by the inequality $\chi(G)\ge \lceil n/\alpha(G)\rceil$ and would follow from the immersion analogue of Hadwiger's conjecture; current results provide weaker lower bounds.
full_parsed_json.source_name: Sebastián Bustamante, Daniel A. Quiroz, Maya Stein and José Zamora, “Clique immersions and independence number”, arXiv:1907.01720 (2022).
full_parsed_json.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.01720

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of July 2019). “The cases $5\le t \le 7$ of Conjecture were established by Lescure and Meyniel and by DeVos, Kawarabayashi, Mohar, and Okamura .”

full_parsed_json.title: Condensed Ricci curvature conjecture for strongly regular conference graphs
full_parsed_json.statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a strongly regular conference graph with parameters

$$
(4\beta+1,2\beta,\beta-1,\beta)
$$

where $\beta\geq 2$. **The condensed Ricci curvature conjecture.** The condensed Ricci curvature satisfies

$$
\Bbbk(x,y)=\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{2\beta}
$$

for every edge $xy\in E$. In particular, every strongly regular conference graph has positive condensed Ricci curvature strictly greater than $\frac{1}{2}$. The conjecture is expected to follow from the matching criterion in the cited theorem if the neighbor sets of every adjacent pair admit perfect matchings; the paper states that this is left for future work.
full_parsed_json.source_name: Vincent Bonini, Conor Carroll, Uyen Dinh, Sydney Dye, Joshua Frederick and Erin Pearse, “Condensed Ricci Curvature of Complete and Strongly Regular Graphs”, arXiv:1907.06733 (2019).
full_parsed_json.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.06733

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2019).

full_parsed_json.title: Common minimal-tree conjecture for totally real algebraic integers
full_parsed_json.statement:
Let $k\in\mathbb{N}$ and let $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_k\in\mathtt{TRAI}\setminus\{0\}$. For each $\lambda_i$, let $\mathcal{T}_{\mathrm{min},\lambda_i}$ denote the set of trees having a nowhere-zero $\lambda_i$-eigenvector.
**Common minimal-tree conjecture.**

$$
\mathcal{T}_{\mathrm{min},\lambda_1}\nsubseteq\mathcal{T}_{\mathrm{min},\lambda_2},\qquad
\bigcap_{i=1}^{k}\mathcal{T}_{\mathrm{min},\lambda_i}\neq\emptyset.
$$

The conjecture asserts both that the first two minimal-tree families are not nested and that one tree can be minimal for all the specified nonzero eigenvalues. The supplied text gives no resolution status.
full_parsed_json.source_name: Asghar Bahmani and Dariush Kiani, “Structure of Trees with Respect to Nodal Vertex Sets”, arXiv:1907.12062 (2020).
full_parsed_json.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.12062

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2019).

full_parsed_json.title: The regularity conjecture for graphs with bounded edge-ideal regularity
full_parsed_json.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph, let $I(G)$ be its edge ideal, and let $G^c$ denote its complement. **Regularity conjecture for graphs with bounded edge-ideal regularity.** If

$$
\operatorname{reg}(I(G))\leq 3
$$

and $G^c$ has no induced $4$-cycle, then

$$
\operatorname{reg}(I(G)^s)=2s
$$

for all $s\geq 2$. The source presents this as a related conjecture and records that analogous stabilization results are known for several graph classes; the stated general case remains open.
full_parsed_json.source_name: Arindam Banerjee and Eran Nevo, “Regularity of Edge Ideals Via Suspension”, arXiv:1908.03115 (2019).
full_parsed_json.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.03115

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2019).

full_parsed_json.title: Existence of uniform posets that are not monoid posets
full_parsed_json.statement:
A **uniform poset** is a poset such that, for every pair of elements $x,y$, the principal upsets ${\uparrow\hspace{-1.5pt}} x$ and ${\uparrow\hspace{-1.5pt}} y$ are order-isomorphic.

**Uniform-poset nonexistence conjecture.** There are uniform posets that are not monoid posets.

Uniformity generalizes the auto-equivalent setting, and the supplied context says that auto-equivalent posets are uniform. The existence of a uniform poset outside the class of monoid posets is presented as a suspicion and remains open in the supplied text.
full_parsed_json.source_name: Ignacio García-Marco, Kolja Knauer and Guillaume Mercui-Voyant, “Cayley posets”, arXiv:1908.09308 (2019).
full_parsed_json.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.09308

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2019).

full_parsed_json.title: Thomassé's cycle-reversion conjecture for dichromatic number
full_parsed_json.statement: Let $D$ be a potentially infinite digraph. A **cycle reversion** reverses the edges of a directed cycle; iteratively perform such reversions, requiring that each edge is reversed only finitely many times, and denote the resulting reorientation by $D^{*}$. **Thomassé's conjecture.** It is possible to choose the reversions so that the dichromatic number of $D^{*}$ is at most two. The conjecture concerns reducing the dichromatic number of arbitrary finite or infinite digraphs through controlled cycle reversions, and its status is open.
full_parsed_json.source_name: Paul Ellis, Attila Joó and Dániel T. Soukup, “Reducing the dichromatic number via cycle reversions in infinite digraphs”, arXiv:1909.00873 (2020).
full_parsed_json.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.00873

Status: **open** according to the source (as of September 2019). “Various old and fascinating questions related to dichromatic number are still open. For example, Neumann-Lara conjectured in that an orientation of a simple planar graph has always dichromatic number at most two.”

full_parsed_json.title: Balogh, Kostochka and Treglown's conjecture on degree sequences forcing perfect clique tilings
full_parsed_json.statement:
Let $n,r\in\mathbb{N}$ with $r$ dividing $n$. Suppose that $G$ is a graph on $n$ vertices with degree sequence $d_1\leq\ldots\leq d_n$ satisfying the following conditions:

$$
d_i\geq (r-2)n/r+i\quad\text{for all }i<n/r;
$$

$$
d_{n/r+1}\geq (r-1)n/r.
$$

**Balogh, Kostochka and Treglown's conjecture.** Then $G$ contains a perfect $K_r$-tiling, that is, a collection of vertex-disjoint copies of $K_r$ covering all vertices of $G$.

This conjecture seeks a degree-sequence condition forcing a perfect $H$-tiling that is best possible in a weaker sense than a Chvátal-type condition. It concerns the degree-sequence analogue of perfect clique-tiling results and remains open in the supplied source context.
full_parsed_json.source_name: Joseph Hyde and Andrew Treglown, “A degree sequence version of the Kühn-Osthus tiling theorem”, arXiv:1909.12670 (2019).
full_parsed_json.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.12670

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2019).

full_parsed_json.title: Duality conjecture for entropic complexity of access structures
full_parsed_json.statement:
Let $P$ be a participant set, let $\mathcal A\subset 2^P$ be an access structure, and let $\mathcal A^\bot$ denote its dual access structure. Let $\sigma(\mathcal A)$ denote the entropic complexity of $\mathcal A$. **Duality conjecture.** For every access structure we have

$$
\sigma(\mathcal A)=\sigma(\mathcal A^\bot).
$$

The analogous equality is known for the polymatroid and linearly representable complexities, while the corresponding statement for entropic complexity is described as a long-standing open problem. The source explicitly says the conjecture is probably not true, so this conjecture is refuted.
full_parsed_json.source_name: Laszlo Csirmaz, “Secret sharing and duality”, arXiv:1909.13663 (2020).
full_parsed_json.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.13663

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of September 2019). “Refuting the second conjecture does not necessarily refutes Conjecture as the dual might be non-ideal while having complexity 1.”

full_parsed_json.title: The lattice equivalence conjecture for facial weak order
full_parsed_json.statement:
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a hyperplane arrangement and let $B$ be a base region of $\mathcal{A}$. Write $\operatorname{PR}$ for the poset of regions and $\operatorname{FW}$ for the facial weak order.

**Lattice equivalence conjecture.** The poset of regions $\operatorname{PR}$ is a lattice if and only if the facial weak order $\operatorname{FW}$ is a lattice.

The forward implication is established in the paper; this conjecture asserts the converse for arbitrary hyperplane arrangements and base regions.
full_parsed_json.source_name: Aram Dermenjian, Christophe Hohlweg, Thomas McConville and Vincent Pilaud, “The facial weak order on hyperplane arrangements”, arXiv:1910.03511 (2019).
full_parsed_json.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.03511

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2019).

full_parsed_json.title: Bang-Jensen et al.'s Meyniel-type conjecture for strong digraphs
full_parsed_json.statement:
Let $D$ be a strong digraph on $n$ vertices. For vertices $u,v$ of $D$, write $d(u)$ and $d(v)$ for their total degrees. Suppose that $u$ and $v$ are non-adjacent and have a common out-neighbour or a common in-neighbour.

**Bang-Jensen et al.'s conjecture.** If

$$
d(u)+d(v)\ge 2n-1
$$

for every such pair $u,v$, then $D$ is hamiltonian.

This conjecture is presented as a strengthening of the classical Meyniel theorem. Its resolution is not established in the supplied text.
full_parsed_json.source_name: Ruixia Wang, Linxin Wu and Wei Meng, “Extremal digraphs on Meyniel-type condition for hamiltonian cycles in balanced bipartite digraphs”, arXiv:1910.05542 (2022).
full_parsed_json.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.05542

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2019).

full_parsed_json.title: K6 and K6,6 sequence rank formula for four-dimensional rigidity
full_parsed_json.statement:
Let $K_n$ be the complete graph and let $F\subseteq E(K_n)$. A proper $\{K_6,K_{6,6}\}$-sequence is the sequence construction defined in the source using copies of $K_6$ and $K_{6,6}$; write $C_{\leq t}$ for the union of its edge sets. **Four-dimensional rank conjecture.** The rank function of ${\cal R}_{4,n}$ is

$$
r(F)=\min\{|F\cup C_{\leq t}|-t:(C_1,\ldots,C_t)\text{ is a proper }\{K_6,K_{6,6}\}\text{-sequence in }K_n\}
$$

for every $F\subseteq E(K_n)$. The conjecture is motivated by the failure of unique maximality for ${\cal R}_{4,n}$, and the source gives no resolution.
full_parsed_json.source_name: Katie Clinch, Bill Jackson and Shin-ichi Tanigawa, “Abstract 3-Rigidity and Bivariate C_2^1-Splines II: Combinatorial Characterization”, arXiv:1911.00207 (2022).
full_parsed_json.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.00207

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2019).

full_parsed_json.title: Characterization of the tableaux-graph order by row entries
full_parsed_json.statement: Let $S,T\in\mathcal{T}(n,n)$ be standard Young tableaux of shape $(n,n)$, and let $a_i$ and $b_i$ denote the entries in the first row of $S$ and $T$, respectively. **Characterization conjecture.** If $a_i\geq b_i$ for all $1\leq i\leq n$, then $S\leq T$ in the tableaux graph. Together with the preceding implication proved in the paper, this would characterize the tableaux-graph order by coordinatewise comparison of first-row entries. The supplied text presents this as part of the proof of the main conjecture and gives no resolution status beyond that presentation.
full_parsed_json.source_name: Mee Seong Im and Jieru Zhu, “Transitioning between tableaux and spider bases for Specht modules”, arXiv:1911.05049 (2020).
full_parsed_json.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.05049

full_parsed_json.title: Compact DV representations for GIRS matrices
full_parsed_json.statement:
Let $(A,\mathbb{G})$ be a GIRS-$c$ pair, and let $\mathbb{V}_\mathbb{G}$ denote the vertex set of $\mathbb{G}$. A **DV representation** is a representation with rank parameters $r_i$ indexed by the vertices. **Compact DV representation conjecture.** If $(A,\mathbb{G})$ is GIRS-$c$, then $(A,\mathbb{G})$ possesses a DV representation with

$$
r_i\leq 2c
$$

for every $i\in\mathbb{V}_\mathbb{G}$. The preceding discussion motivates compact representations, but the source gives no evidence that this conjecture has been resolved.
full_parsed_json.source_name: Shivkumar Chandrasekaran, Ethan N. Epperly and Nithin Govindarajan, “Graph-Induced Rank Structures and their Representations”, arXiv:1911.05858 (2021).
full_parsed_json.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.05858

full_parsed_json.title: De Loera et al.'s Ehrhart positivity conjecture for matroid polytopes
full_parsed_json.statement: Let $M$ be a matroid, and let $\mathscr{P}(M)$ denote its basis polytope. Its Ehrhart polynomial is the polynomial counting lattice points in integer dilations of $\mathscr{P}(M)$. **De Loera et al.'s conjecture.** The coefficients of the Ehrhart polynomial of $\mathscr{P}(M)$ are positive. This conjecture was posed for matroid basis polytopes and is motivated by Ehrhart-positivity questions in combinatorics. The paper proves the assertion for all hypersimplices, which are the basis polytopes of uniform matroids; the general matroid case is not resolved here.
full_parsed_json.source_name: Luis Ferroni, “Hypersimplices are Ehrhart Positive”, arXiv:1911.10146 (2020).
full_parsed_json.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.10146

Status: **open** according to the source (as of November 2019). “For example, the unimodality of its coefficients is still an open problem . Recently the author conjectured that the $h^*$-polynomial of all matroid polytopes (in particular of hypersimplices) are real-rooted .”

full_parsed_json.title: The multiple-free subset-sum conjecture for powers of two
full_parsed_json.statement:
Let $z\in\mathbb{N}$ and let $A=\{a_1,\ldots,a_k\}\subseteq[2^z]$, where $[2^z]=\{1,2,\ldots,2^z\}$. For each non-empty subset $A_i$ of $A$, write $S(A_i)$ for the sum of its elements. **Multiple-free subset-sum conjecture.** If for every $i,j\le 2^k-1$ the quotient

$$
\frac{S(A_i)}{S(A_j)}
$$

is not a power of $2$, then

$$
k=z+O\left(1\right).
$$

The condition says that the subset sums form a multiple-free sequence with respect to powers of $2$. The conjecture is motivated by numerical data and would sharpen the known lower-bound constructions for this problem; the paper does not provide a proof or resolution.
full_parsed_json.source_name: Konstantinos Gaitanas, “Two divisibility problems on subset sums”, arXiv:1911.11097 (2019).
full_parsed_json.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.11097

Status: **open** according to the source (as of November 2019).

full_parsed_json.title: The symmetric chain decomposition extension conjecture for hypercubes
full_parsed_json.statement: A **symmetric chain decomposition** (SCD) of the hypercube $Q_n$ is a partition of its vertices into symmetric chains, where a symmetric chain is a path $(x_k,x_{k+1},\ldots,x_{n-k})$ such that $x_i$ lies at level $i$ for every $k\leq i\leq n-k$. **The symmetric chain decomposition extension conjecture.** Every SCD can be extended to a Hamilton cycle in $Q_n$. This conjecture extends results of Streib and Trotter and the Greene–Kleitman construction, which show that particular SCDs can be extended to Hamilton cycles. It is motivated by the conjecture of Ruskey and Savage that every matching in $Q_n$ extends to a Hamilton cycle.
full_parsed_json.source_name: Petr Gregor, Ondřej Mička and Torsten Mütze, “On the central levels problem”, arXiv:1912.01566 (2021).
full_parsed_json.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.01566

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2019).

full_parsed_json.title: Criticality conjecture for interlacing edges of large Schrijver graphs
full_parsed_json.statement: Let $d$ be any integer, let $k_d$ be a threshold depending on $d$, and let ${\rm SG}(2k+d,k)$ be the Schrijver graph. An edge is **interlacing** according to the standard interlacing-edge definition for Schrijver graphs, and an edge is **critical** if deleting it lowers the chromatic number. **Interlacing-edge criticality conjecture.** For every $d$ and every $k>k_d$, all interlacing edges of ${\rm SG}(2k+d,k)$ are critical. This would characterize the critical edges for Schrijver graphs of large size with fixed small chromatic-number excess, extending the corresponding theorem cited in the source; the full characterization of critical edges is not known.
full_parsed_json.source_name: Gábor Simonyi and Gábor Tardos, “On 4-chromatic Schrijver graphs: their structure, non-3-colorability, and critical edges”, arXiv:1912.03724 (2019).
full_parsed_json.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.03724

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2019).

full_parsed_json.title: The three-weight sum-set characterization for odd sums
full_parsed_json.statement:
Let $C(\Omega)^\bot$ be a code of length $n$ with three nonzero weights $w_1<w_2<w_3$, where $p$ is prime and $m$ is a positive integer. The weights are related to an $s$-sum set $\Omega$ as in the paper.

**The three-weight sum-set conjecture.** $\Omega$ is an $s$-sum set for some $s>3$ if and only if

$$
(w_1,w_2,w_3)=\left(w_1,n(p-1)p^{m-2},2n(p-1)p^{m-2}-w_1\right),
$$

for some $0<w_1<n(p-1)p^{m-2}$.

This claim characterizes the three-weight configurations that can arise from an $s$-sum set with $s>3$, extending the preceding results that identify a symmetric weight configuration yielding $s$-sum sets for every odd $s>1$. The supplied text does not indicate whether the claim has been proved or disproved.
full_parsed_json.source_name: Michael Kiermaier, Sascha Kurz, Minjia Shi and Patrick Solé, “Three-weight codes over rings and strongly walk regular graphs”, arXiv:1912.03892 (2019).
full_parsed_json.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.03892

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2019).

full_parsed_json.title: Schmutz Schaller's automorphism conjecture for the Schmutz Schaller curve graph
full_parsed_json.statement:
Let $S$ be the surface under consideration, and let $\mathcal{SC}(S)$ denote the Schmutz Schaller curve graph, with vertices and edges as defined in the paper. Let $\operatorname{Mod}^{\pm}(S)$ be the extended mapping class group of $S$. **Schmutz Schaller's conjecture.** The automorphism group of $\mathcal{SC}(S)$ is isomorphic to

$$
\operatorname{Mod}^{\pm}(S).
$$

Schmutz Schaller proposed this conjecture for the automorphism group of the curve graph, and the paper resolves it for all but the cases $(g,p)=(1,3)$ and $(g,p)=(0,5)$, so the general statement remains open in those exceptional cases.
full_parsed_json.source_name: Shuchi Agrawal, Tarik Aougab, Yassin Chandran, Marissa Loving, J. Robert Oakley, Roberta Shapiro and Yang Xiao, “Automorphisms of the k-curve graph”, arXiv:1912.07666 (2023).
full_parsed_json.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.07666

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2019).
